title.zh: 卷143 志一百十八 刑法二
title.raw: 卷143 志一百十八 刑法二

sentences.zh: 志一百十八

translations.literal: Treatise Number 118
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 118

sentences.zh: 刑法二

translations.literal: Penal Law, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Penal Law 2

sentences.zh: 明律淵源唐代，以笞、杖、徒、流、死為五刑。

translations.literal: The Ming Code traced its origins to the Tang dynasty, taking beating with the light bamboo, beating with the heavy stick, penal servitude, exile, and death as the five punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming legal code derived from Tang practice and recognized five punishments: light-bamboo beating, heavy-stick beating, penal servitude, exile, and death.

sentences.zh: 自笞一十至五十，為笞刑五。

translations.literal: From ten blows of the light bamboo to fifty, these were the five grades of light-bamboo punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Light-bamboo punishments comprised five grades, from ten to fifty blows.

sentences.zh: 自杖六十至一百，為杖刑五。

translations.literal: From sixty blows of the heavy stick to one hundred, these were the five grades of stick beating.
translations.idiomatic: Stick beating likewise had five grades, ranging from sixty to one hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 徒自杖六十徒一年起，每等加杖十，刑期半年，至杖一百徒三年，為徒五等。

translations.literal: Penal servitude began with sixty blows and one year of service; each grade added ten blows and half a year to the term, up to one hundred blows and three years of service, making five grades of servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude started at sixty blows plus one year's labor; each step added ten blows and six months, culminating at one hundred blows with three years' service—five grades in all.

sentences.zh: 流以二千里、二千五百里、三千里為三等，而皆加杖一百。

translations.literal: Exile was divided into three grades at two thousand, two thousand five hundred, and three thousand li, and in each case one hundred blows of the stick were added.
translations.idiomatic: Exile had three distances—two thousand, two thousand five hundred, and three thousand li—and each grade included an additional hundred stick blows.

sentences.zh: 死刑二：曰斬，曰絞。

translations.literal: There were two capital punishments: decapitation and strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment took two forms: decapitation and strangulation.

sentences.zh: 此正刑也。

translations.literal: These were the orthodox punishments.
translations.idiomatic: These constituted the formal statutory punishments.

sentences.zh: 其律例內之雜犯、斬絞、遷徙、充軍、枷號、刺字、論贖、凌遲、梟首、戮屍等刑，或取諸前代，或明所自創，要皆非刑之正。

translations.literal: Within the statutes and sub-statutes there were also such punishments as miscellaneous offenses subject to decapitation or strangulation, removal and resettlement, military exile, wearing the cangue, tattooing, commutation by payment, lingchi, exposure of the severed head, and dismemberment of the corpse; some were drawn from earlier dynasties and some were Ming innovations—in every case they were not among the orthodox punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The code and its supplementary statutes also prescribed decapitation and strangulation for miscellaneous crimes, resettlement, military exile, the cangue, tattooing, ransom payments, lingchi, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment—some inherited from earlier dynasties, others a Ming creation—all of them punishments outside the formal five-penalty framework.

sentences.zh: 清太祖、太宗之治遼東，刑制尚簡，重則斬，輕則鞭撲而已。

translations.literal: Under the Taizu and Taizong emperors of the Qing, when they ruled the eastern Liao region, the penal system was still simple: serious cases were punished by decapitation, light ones by whipping and beating only.
translations.idiomatic: During the early Qing rule of the eastern Liao under the Taizu and Taizong emperors, penal law remained simple: serious offenses meant decapitation, minor ones no more than whipping and beating.

sentences.zh: 迨世祖入關，沿襲明制，初頒刑律，笞、杖以五折十，注入本刑各條。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor entered the pass and took the throne, he followed the Ming system and first promulgated the penal code; light-bamboo and stick punishments were calculated on the principle of counting five blows as ten, and this was inserted into the articles on each principal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu emperor crossed into China proper, the Qing adopted Ming practice and issued its first penal code, applying the five-for-ten reduction to light-bamboo and stick penalties and embedding it in the relevant articles.

sentences.zh: 康熙朝現行則例改為四折除零。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign the current sub-statutes changed this to a fourfold reduction with odd numbers dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, the operative sub-statutes replaced this with a fourfold reduction, dropping remainders.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年之律，乃依例各於本律註明板數。

translations.literal: The code of the third year of the Yongzheng reign, following the sub-statutes, noted the number of blows in each relevant article of the principal code.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng code of 1725, following sub-statutory practice, specified the exact number of blows in each principal article.

sentences.zh: 徒、流加杖，亦至配所照數折責。

translations.literal: For penal servitude and exile, the additional stick blows were also reduced according to the prescribed number upon arrival at the place of assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Additional stick blows attached to servitude and exile were likewise reduced to the prescribed count once the convict reached his place of assignment.

sentences.zh: 蓋恐撲責過多，致傷生命，法外之仁也。

translations.literal: This was because they feared that excessive beating and flogging might endanger life—an act of mercy beyond what the letter of the law required.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to avoid so much beating that life was endangered—a mercy extending beyond strict legal requirement.

sentences.zh: 文武官犯笞、杖，則分別公私，代以罰俸、降級、降調，至革職而止。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials incurred light-bamboo or stick punishment, public and private offenses were distinguished, and in place of physical punishment they received salary fines, demotion in rank, or transfer to a lower post, up to dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials subject to light-bamboo or stick penalties were treated according to whether the offense was public or private: fines, demotion, transfer, or dismissal replaced corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 徒者，奴也，蓋奴辱之。

translations.literal: Penal servitude (tu) means to be made a slave; it was essentially servitude intended to humiliate.
translations.idiomatic: Penal servitude—the word tu means slave—was essentially compulsory labor meant to degrade the offender.

sentences.zh: 明發鹽場鐵冶煎鹽炒鐵，清則發本省驛遞。

translations.literal: Under the Ming, convicts were sent to salt works and iron smelteries to boil salt and smelt iron; under the Qing they were assigned to the courier stations within their own province.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming sent convicts to salt pans and ironworks for salt boiling and iron smelting; the Qing assigned them to courier service within their home province.

sentences.zh: 其無驛縣，分撥各衙門充水火夫各項雜役，限滿釋放。

translations.literal: In counties without courier stations, they were distributed among various yamens to serve as water carriers, fire tenders, and other miscellaneous laborers, and released when the term expired.
translations.idiomatic: Where no courier stations existed, convicts were allotted to government offices as water carriers, fire tenders, and other menial laborers and released when their term ended.

sentences.zh: 流犯，初制由各縣解交巡撫衙門，按照里數，酌發各處荒蕪及瀕海州縣。

translations.literal: Exiled convicts were at first, under the original system, sent up from the counties to the provincial governor's yamen; according to the distance in li, they were assigned as appropriate to desolate or coastal prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, exiled convicts were forwarded from county to provincial governor's office and, according to the statutory distance, assigned to desolate or coastal districts.

sentences.zh: 嗣以各省分撥失均，不免趨避揀擇。

translations.literal: Later, because distribution among the provinces was uneven, there was inevitably evasion and selective preference.
translations.idiomatic: Uneven distribution among provinces soon led to evasion and cherry-picking of destinations.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，刑部始纂輯三流道里表，將某省某府屬流犯，應流二千里者發何省何府屬安置，應流二千五百里者發何省何府屬安置，應流三千里者發何省何府屬安置，按計程途，限定地址，逐省逐府，分別開載。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Qianlong reign the Board of Punishments first compiled a table of routes and distances for the three grades of exile, specifying for convicts from such-and-such a province and prefecture who were to be exiled two thousand li which province and prefecture they were to be sent to for resettlement, likewise for those exiled two thousand five hundred li and three thousand li; distances were calculated, destinations fixed, and entries listed separately province by province and prefecture by prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1743 the Board of Punishments compiled a table of exile routes and distances, assigning convicts from each province and prefecture to specific destinations for the two-thousand-, two-thousand-five-hundred-, and three-thousand-li grades, with distances calculated and every province and prefecture listed in detail.

sentences.zh: 嗣於四十九年及嘉慶六年兩次修訂。

translations.literal: It was revised twice thereafter, in the forty-ninth year of Qianlong and the sixth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: The table was revised twice more, in 1784 and 1801.

sentences.zh: 然第於州縣之增並，道里之參差，略有修改，而大體不易。

translations.literal: However, apart from slight modifications owing to the merging or splitting of prefectures and counties and discrepancies in distances, the overall framework remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Revisions were limited to administrative mergers and minor distance adjustments; the overall scheme stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 律稱：「犯流妻妾從之，父祖子孫欲隨者聽。」

translations.literal: The code states: "When one is exiled, wife and concubines follow; if father, grandfather, sons, or grandsons wish to accompany him, permission is granted."
translations.idiomatic: The code provided: "When a man is exiled, his wife and concubines accompany him; fathers, grandfathers, sons, and grandsons may follow if they wish."

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十四年，將僉妻之例停止。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of the Qianlong reign the regulation requiring wives to accompany was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In 1759 the requirement that wives accompany exiled convicts was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其軍、流、遣犯情原隨帶家屬者，不得官為資送，律成虛設矣。

translations.literal: As for military exiles, banished convicts, and those sent into frontier banishment who wished in principle to bring their families, the state no longer provided official transport—and the statute became a dead letter.
translations.idiomatic: Convicts in military exile, banishment, or frontier deportation who wished to bring their families received no official assistance, rendering the statutory provision meaningless.

sentences.zh: 斬、絞，同是死刑。

translations.literal: Decapitation and strangulation were alike capital punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Decapitation and strangulation were both capital punishments.

sentences.zh: 然自漢以來，有秋後決囚之制。

translations.literal: Yet since the Han dynasty there had been the institution of executing prisoners after the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han, however, there had been the practice of carrying out executions only after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 唐律除犯惡逆以上及奴婢、部曲殺主者，從立春至秋分不得奏決死刑。

translations.literal: The Tang Code, except for those guilty of treason and above, and for slaves, bondsmen, or retainers who killed their master, forbade reporting capital sentences for execution from the Beginning of Spring to the Autumn Equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, capital cases could not be reported for execution between the Beginning of Spring and the Autumn Equinox, except for treason and for slaves or retainers who killed their master.

sentences.zh: 明弘治十年奏定真犯死罪決不待時者，凌遲十二條，斬三十七條，絞十二條；

translations.literal: In the tenth year of the Hongzhi reign of the Ming it was memorialized and fixed that for true capital offenses to be executed without waiting for the season: lingchi twelve articles, decapitation thirty-seven articles, strangulation twelve articles;
translations.idiomatic: In 1497 the Ming fixed immediate execution for true capital crimes: twelve articles of lingchi, thirty-seven of decapitation, and twelve of strangulation;

sentences.zh: 真犯死罪秋後處決者，斬一百條，絞八十六條。

translations.literal: for true capital offenses to be executed after autumn: decapitation one hundred articles, strangulation eighty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: capital crimes deferred until after autumn: one hundred articles of decapitation and eighty-six of strangulation.

sentences.zh: 順治初定律，乃於各條內分晰註明，凡律不注監候者，皆立決也；

translations.literal: When the code was first established in the early Shunzhi reign, each article was clearly annotated within it: wherever the code did not note "await execution in custody," all were immediate execution;
translations.idiomatic: The early Shunzhi code annotated each article clearly: unless marked for detention pending review, every capital offense was immediate execution;

sentences.zh: 凡例不言立決者，皆監候也。

translations.literal: wherever the sub-statutes did not say "immediate execution," all were held in custody awaiting review.
translations.idiomatic: where sub-statutes did not specify immediate execution, all were held for autumn review.

sentences.zh: 自此京、外死罪多決於秋，朝審遂為一代之大典。

translations.literal: From this time onward most capital cases in the capital and in the provinces were decided in autumn, and the court review of capital cases became a great institution of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter most capital sentences in the capital and provinces were carried out in autumn, and the annual court review of death cases became a defining institution of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 雜犯斬、絞准徒五年與雜犯三流總徒四年，大都創自有明。

translations.literal: For miscellaneous offenses, decapitation and strangulation were commuted to five years of penal servitude, and the three grades of exile for miscellaneous offenses totaled four years of servitude—most of these were Ming innovations.
translations.idiomatic: Commutation of miscellaneous capital offenses to five years' servitude and of miscellaneous exile to four years' servitude were largely Ming innovations.

sentences.zh: 清律於官吏受贓，枉法不枉法，滿貫俱改為實絞，餘多仍之。

translations.literal: In the Qing code, for officials who accepted bribes, whether or not they perverted the law, when the full quota was reached all were changed to actual strangulation; most other provisions were retained.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing code made actual strangulation mandatory for officials who took bribes to the full statutory amount, whether or not they had perverted justice, while retaining most other Ming provisions.

sentences.zh: 名實混淆，殊形轇轕。

translations.literal: Names and realities were confused, and the provisions became tangled in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Legal labels and actual penalties diverged, producing extreme confusion.

sentences.zh: 遷徙原於唐之殺人移鄉，而定罪則異。

translations.literal: Removal and resettlement originated in the Tang practice of transferring murderers to another district, but the determination of guilt differed.
translations.idiomatic: Resettlement derived from the Tang practice of relocating murderers to another district, but the grounds for conviction differed.

sentences.zh: 律文沿用數條，然皆改為比流減半、徒二年，並不徙諸千里之外。

translations.literal: Several articles of the code text were retained, but all were changed to half the distance of exile and two years of penal servitude, and did not involve removal a thousand li or more.
translations.idiomatic: Several statutory articles survived, but all were reduced to half the exile distance plus two years' servitude, without relocation a thousand li or more.

sentences.zh: 惟條例於土蠻、瑤、僮、苗人仇殺劫擄及改土為流之土司有犯，將家口實行遷徙。

translations.literal: Only in the sub-statutes, for Tujia, Yao, Zhuang, and Miao who committed feud killings, robbery, and abduction, and for native chieftains whose domains had been converted to regular administration, were the offender's household actually resettled.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-statutes alone required actual resettlement of entire families for feud killings, robbery, and abduction among Tujia, Yao, Zhuang, and Miao peoples, and for native chieftains in converted territories who committed crimes.

sentences.zh: 然各有定地，亦不限千里也。

translations.literal: Yet each had a fixed destination, and the distance was not limited to a thousand li either.
translations.idiomatic: Each case had a designated destination, and distances were not necessarily a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 明之充軍，義主實邊，不盡與流刑相比附。

translations.literal: Ming military exile was chiefly intended to strengthen the frontier and did not wholly correspond to the exile punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Ming military exile was meant chiefly to reinforce the frontier and did not always align with statutory exile.

sentences.zh: 清初裁撤邊衛，而仍沿充軍之名。

translations.literal: In the early Qing the frontier garrisons were abolished, yet the name military exile was retained.
translations.idiomatic: The early Qing abolished frontier garrisons but kept the term military exile.

sentences.zh: 後遂以附近、近邊、邊遠、極邊、煙瘴為五軍，且於滿流以上，為節級加等之用。

translations.literal: Later there came to be five grades of military exile—nearby, near the frontier, distant frontier, extreme frontier, and miasma regions—and for offenses above the full statutory exile distance they served to add graded increases.
translations.idiomatic: Five grades of military exile emerged—nearby, near frontier, distant frontier, extreme frontier, and miasma regions—used to escalate penalties beyond full statutory exile.

sentences.zh: 附近二千里，近邊二千五百里，邊遠三千里，極邊、煙瘴俱四千里。

translations.literal: Nearby was two thousand li, near the frontier two thousand five hundred li, distant frontier three thousand li, extreme frontier and miasma regions each four thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Distances were two thousand li for nearby, two thousand five hundred for near frontier, three thousand for distant frontier, and four thousand for extreme frontier and miasma regions.

sentences.zh: 在京兵部定地，在外巡撫定地。

translations.literal: In the capital the Board of War fixed the place of assignment; in the provinces the provincial governor fixed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of War assigned destinations in the capital; provincial governors did so in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年之律，第於十五布政司應發省分約略編定。

translations.literal: The code of the third year of Yongzheng only roughly compiled which provinces among the fifteen provincial administrations should receive convicts.
translations.idiomatic: The 1725 code only roughly specified which of the fifteen provincial administrations should receive convicts.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年，兵部根據邦政紀略，輯為五軍道里表，凡發配者，視表所列。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong the Board of War, drawing on the Records of Frontier Administration, compiled a table of routes and distances for the five grades of military exile; all who were sent into exile were assigned according to what the table listed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1772 the Board of War compiled a table of military-exile routes and distances from frontier administration records; all assignments followed the table.

sentences.zh: 然名為充軍，至配並不入營差操，第於每月朔望檢點，實與流犯無異。

translations.literal: Yet though called military exile, upon assignment they did not enter camps for duty or drill but were merely checked on the first and fifteenth of each month—in reality no different from banished convicts.
translations.idiomatic: Despite the name, military exiles never joined garrison duty or drill; they were checked only on the first and fifteenth of each month and were in practice indistinguishable from banished convicts.

sentences.zh: 而滿流加附近、近邊道里，反由遠而近，司讞者每苦其紛歧，而又有發遣名目。

translations.literal: Yet when full exile was increased to nearby or near-frontier military exile, the distance ran from far to near in reverse, and those who judged cases were often troubled by the confusion; moreover there was the separate category of frontier deportation.
translations.idiomatic: Escalating full exile to nearby or near-frontier military exile reversed distances from far to near, baffling judges; a further category of frontier deportation added to the confusion.

sentences.zh: 初第發尚陽堡、寧古塔，或烏喇地方安插，後並發齊齊哈爾、黑龍江、三姓、喀爾喀、科布多，或各省駐防為奴。

translations.literal: At first they were sent only to Shangyang Fort, Ningguta, or settled in the Ula region; later they were also sent to Qiqihar, Heilongjiang, Sanxing, Khalkha, Kobdo, or assigned as slaves to garrisons in the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Initially deportees went only to Shangyang Fort, Ningguta, or the Ula region; later destinations included Qiqihar, Heilongjiang, Sanxing, Khalkha, Kobdo, or enslavement in provincial garrisons.

sentences.zh: 乾隆年間，新疆開闢，例又有發往伊犁、烏魯木齊、巴里坤各回城分別為奴種地者。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, when Xinjiang was opened, sub-statutes also provided for sending convicts to Yili, Urumqi, Barkol, and various Muslim towns to serve as slaves tilling the land.
translations.idiomatic: After Xinjiang was opened in the Qianlong era, convicts could also be sent to Yili, Urumqi, Barkol, and Muslim towns as bonded laborers on the land.

sentences.zh: 咸、同之際，新疆道梗，又復改發內地充軍。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, when routes to Xinjiang were blocked, assignment reverted to military exile within the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinjiang routes were cut off in the Xianfeng and Tongzhi periods, convicts were again assigned to military exile within China proper.

sentences.zh: 其制屢經變易，然軍遣止及其身。

translations.literal: The system underwent many changes, yet military exile and deportation extended only to the offender himself.
translations.idiomatic: The system changed repeatedly, but military exile and deportation applied only to the offender himself.

sentences.zh: 苟情節稍輕，尚得更赦放還。

translations.literal: If the circumstances were somewhat lighter, they might still be released through repeated amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: Where circumstances were relatively mild, repeated amnesties could still secure release.

sentences.zh: 以視明之永遠軍戍，數世後猶句及本籍子孫者，大有間也。

translations.literal: Compared with the Ming practice of perpetual military garrison service, in which generations later descendants in the native place were still implicated, the difference was very great.
translations.idiomatic: This differed greatly from Ming perpetual military service, which could still implicate descendants in the offender's home district generations later.

sentences.zh: 若文武職官犯徒以上，輕則軍台效力，重則新疆當差。

translations.literal: If civil or military officials committed offenses above penal servitude, in lighter cases they served at courier stations; in heavier cases they performed labor in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials guilty of offenses above penal servitude served at courier stations for lighter cases and performed labor in Xinjiang for heavier ones.

sentences.zh: 成案相沿，遂為定例。

translations.literal: As precedents accumulated case by case, this became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated precedent made this standard practice.

sentences.zh: 此又軍遣中之歧出者焉。

translations.literal: This was yet another exceptional branch within military exile and deportation.
translations.idiomatic: This was yet another exceptional variant within military exile and deportation.

sentences.zh: 枷杻，本以羈獄囚。

translations.literal: The cangue and fetters were originally used to restrain prisoners in jail.
translations.idiomatic: The cangue and fetters were originally meant to restrain jail prisoners.

sentences.zh: 明代問刑條例，於本罪外或加以枷號，示戮辱也。

translations.literal: The Ming Interrogation and Punishment Sub-statutes sometimes added wearing the cangue beyond the principal offense, to display shame and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Ming interrogation sub-statutes sometimes added cangue wearing beyond the principal sentence as public humiliation.

sentences.zh: 清律犯罪免發遣條：「凡旗人犯罪，笞、杖各照數鞭責，軍、流、徒免發遣，分別枷號。

translations.literal: The Qing code article on crimes exempt from deportation states: "Whenever a Bannerman commits a crime, light-bamboo and stick punishments are administered by whipping according to the full number; military exile, banishment, and penal servitude are exempt from actual deportation and replaced by wearing the cangue according to grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing statute on exempting Bannermen from deportation reads: "Bannermen who commit offenses receive full light-bamboo or stick whipping; military exile, banishment, and penal servitude are commuted to graded cangue wearing instead of actual deportation.

sentences.zh: 徒一年者，枷號二十日，每等遞加五日。

translations.literal: For one year of penal servitude, twenty days in the cangue; each grade adds five days.
translations.idiomatic: One year of servitude meant twenty days in the cangue, with five days added per grade.

sentences.zh: 流二千里者，枷號五十日，每等亦遞加五日。

translations.literal: For exile of two thousand li, fifty days in the cangue; each grade likewise adds five days.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thousand-li exile meant fifty days in the cangue, with five days added per grade.

sentences.zh: 充軍附近者，枷號七十日，近邊、沿海、邊外者八十日，極邊、煙瘴者九十日。」

translations.literal: For nearby military exile, seventy days in the cangue; for near frontier, coastal, and outer frontier, eighty days; for extreme frontier and miasma regions, ninety days."
translations.idiomatic: Nearby military exile meant seventy days in the cangue; near frontier, coastal, and outer frontier eighty days; extreme frontier and miasma regions ninety days."

sentences.zh: 原立法之意，亦以旗人生則入檔，壯則充兵，鞏衛本根，未便離遠，有犯徒、流等罪，直以枷號代刑，強榦之義則然。

translations.literal: The original legislative intent was also that Bannermen were registered at birth and served as soldiers in adulthood, guarding the dynastic root; it was inconvenient to send them far away, and when they committed penal servitude, exile, and the like, the cangue was used directly in place of punishment—thus strengthening the trunk, as the principle required.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was that Bannermen were registered at birth and served as soldiers in adulthood to guard the dynasty's foundation; sending them far away was undesirable, so the cangue replaced servitude and exile—strengthening the trunk, as the principle required.

sentences.zh: 然犯系寡廉鮮恥，則銷除旗檔，一律實發，不姑息也。

translations.literal: Yet when the offense involved gross want of shame, the Banner register was struck off and full deportation was imposed without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: For offenses showing gross moral corruption, however, Banner registration was revoked and full deportation imposed without leniency.

sentences.zh: 若竊盜再犯加枷，初犯再犯計次加枷，犯奸加枷，賭博加枷，逃軍逃流加枷，暨一切敗檢逾閒、不顧行止者酌量加枷，則初無旗、民之別。

translations.literal: For repeat theft the cangue was added; for first and repeat offenses the cangue was increased by count; for adultery, gambling, desertion from military exile or banishment, and for all who breached propriety and disregarded conduct, discretionary additional cangue was imposed—and in these cases there was originally no distinction between Bannermen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat theft, counted first and repeat offenses, adultery, gambling, desertion from exile, and all breaches of propriety drew additional cangue penalties with no distinction between Bannermen and commoners.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，部議囚禁人犯止用細鍊，不用長枷，而枷號遂專為行刑之用。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi the ministry deliberated that imprisoned convicts should use only light chains, not the long cangue, and wearing the cangue then became exclusively a means of carrying out punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1669 the ministry ruled that prisoners should be restrained with light chains only, not the long cangue, and cangue wearing became exclusively a punitive measure.

sentences.zh: 其數初不過一月、二月、三月，後竟有論年或永遠枷號者。

translations.literal: At first the duration was no more than one, two, or three months; later there were even cases measured in years or perpetual cangue wearing.
translations.idiomatic: Terms initially ran no longer than one to three months; later some lasted years or even indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 始制重者七十觔，輕者六十斤。

translations.literal: Under the original system the heavy cangue weighed seventy jin and the light one sixty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the heavy cangue weighed seventy jin and the light one sixty.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五年，改定應枷人犯俱重二十五斤，然例尚有用百斤重枷者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianlong it was revised that all who were to wear the cangue should bear twenty-five jin, yet sub-statutes still provided for a hundred-jin heavy cangue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1740 all cangues were standardized at twenty-five jin, though sub-statutes still allowed a hundred-jin heavy cangue.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶以降，重枷斷用三十五斤，而於四川、陝西、湖北、河南、山東、安徽、廣東等省匪徒，又有系帶鐵杆石礅之例，亦一時創刑也。

translations.literal: From the Jiaqing reign onward the heavy cangue was fixed at thirty-five jin; in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Anhui, Guangdong, and other provinces, for bandits there was also the practice of attaching an iron rod and stone block—another punitive innovation of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jiaqing era onward, the heavy cangue was fixed at thirty-five jin; in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Henan, Shandong, Anhui, Guangdong, and other provinces, bandits could also be fitted with iron rods and stone blocks, another ad hoc punishment of the age.

sentences.zh: 刺字，古肉刑之一，律第嚴於賊盜。

translations.literal: Tattooing was one of the ancient corporal punishments; in the code it was applied most strictly to thieves and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing was an ancient corporal punishment; the code applied it most strictly to thieves and robbers.

sentences.zh: 乃其後條例滋多，刺緣坐，刺兇犯，刺逃軍、逃流，刺外遣、改遣、改發。

translations.literal: Later sub-statutes multiplied: tattooing for guilt by association, for violent offenders, for deserters from military exile and banishment, for those sent into outer deportation, re-deportation, or re-assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Later sub-statutes multiplied: tattooing for guilt by association, violent offenders, deserters from exile, and those in outer deportation or reassignment.

sentences.zh: 有刺事由者，有刺地方者，並有分刺滿、漢文字者。

translations.literal: Some tattoos recorded the reason for the offense, some the place, and some were inscribed separately in Manchu and Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: Some tattoos recorded the offense, some the place, and some were inscribed in both Manchu and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 初刺右臂，次刺左臂，次刺右面、左面。

translations.literal: The first tattoo was on the right arm, the next on the left arm, then on the right cheek and left cheek.
translations.idiomatic: The first tattoo went on the right arm, then the left arm, then the right and left cheeks.

sentences.zh: 大抵律多刺臂，例多刺面。

translations.literal: Generally the code mostly tattooed the arms, while sub-statutes mostly tattooed the face.
translations.idiomatic: The code generally tattooed the arms; sub-statutes more often tattooed the face.

sentences.zh: 若竊盜責充警跡，二三年無過，或緝獲強盜二名以上、竊盜三名以上，例又准其起除刺字，復為良民。

translations.literal: If a thief was required to serve as a police tracker, and after two or three years committed no offense, or apprehended two or more robbers or three or more thieves, sub-statutes also permitted removal of the tattoo and restoration as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves assigned as police trackers who went two or three years without offense, or who captured two robbers or three thieves, could have their tattoos removed and regain commoner status.

sentences.zh: 蓋惡惡雖嚴，而亦未嘗不予以自新之路焉。

translations.literal: Thus although hatred of evil was severe, a path to reform was never wholly denied.
translations.idiomatic: Though punishment of evil was severe, a path to reform was never wholly closed.

sentences.zh: 贖刑有三：一曰納贖，無力照律決配，有力照例納贖。

translations.literal: There were three kinds of commutation by payment: first, payment commutation—those without means were sentenced and assigned according to the code; those with means paid commutation according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Commutation took three forms: payment commutation, under which the poor were sentenced as the code required and the wealthy paid ransom according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 二曰收贖，老幼廢疾、天文生及婦人折杖，照律收贖。

translations.literal: Second, statutory commutation—the aged, young, disabled, students of astronomy, and women subject to reduced stick beating commuted according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: Second, statutory commutation allowed the aged, young, disabled, astronomy students, and women subject to reduced beating to commute according to the code.

sentences.zh: 三曰贖罪，官員正妻及例難的決，並婦人有力者，照例贖罪。

translations.literal: Third, offense commutation—officials' principal wives and cases where sub-statutes forbade actual execution, as well as women with means, commuted offenses according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Third, offense commutation covered officials' principal wives, cases where sub-statutes forbade execution, and women of means.

sentences.zh: 收贖名曰律贖，原本唐律收贖。

translations.literal: Statutory commutation was called code commutation and originated in the Tang Code's statutory commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory commutation, called code commutation, derived from Tang practice.

sentences.zh: 贖罪名為例贖，則明代所創行。

translations.literal: Offense commutation, called sub-statutory commutation, was a Ming innovation.
translations.idiomatic: Offense commutation, or sub-statutory commutation, was a Ming innovation.

sentences.zh: 順治修律，五刑不列贖銀數目。

translations.literal: When the code was revised in the Shunzhi reign, the five punishments did not list the amounts of silver for commutation.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi code revision omitted silver amounts for commutation of the five punishments.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，始將明律贖圖內應贖銀數斟酌修改，定為納贖諸例圖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng the amounts of silver for commutation in the Ming commutation charts were revised after deliberation and fixed as the charts for payment commutation sub-statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1725 the Ming commutation charts were revised to establish the payment commutation tables.

sentences.zh: 然自康熙現行例定有承問官濫准納贖交部議處之條，而前明納贖及贖罪諸舊例又節經刪改，故律贖俱照舊援用，而例贖則多成具文。

translations.literal: Yet since the Kangxi current sub-statutes provided that examining officials who improperly approved payment commutation were to be referred to the ministry for disciplinary action, and the old Ming provisions on payment commutation and offense commutation had been repeatedly revised and cut, code commutation was all applied according to the old practice, while sub-statutory commutation largely became dead letter.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kangxi sub-statutes penalized officials who improperly approved payment commutation, and Ming provisions on payment and offense commutation had been repeatedly trimmed, code commutation continued under old rules while sub-statutory commutation largely became a dead letter.

sentences.zh: 其捐贖一項，順治十八年，有官員犯流徒籍沒認工贖罪例；

translations.literal: As for the item of donation commutation, in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi there was a precedent for officials guilty of exile or penal servitude to have their property confiscated and to redeem their offense by undertaking labor;
translations.idiomatic: Donation commutation began in 1661 with a precedent allowing officials guilty of exile or servitude to redeem offenses through labor after confiscation;

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，有死罪現監人犯輸米邊口贖罪例；

translations.literal: in the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi there was a precedent for capital convicts presently in custody to redeem their offense by delivering grain to the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: in 1690 capital convicts in custody could redeem offenses by delivering grain to the frontier;

sentences.zh: 三十年，有軍流人犯捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirtieth year, a precedent for military exiles and banished convicts to redeem by donation;
translations.idiomatic: in 1691 military exiles and banished convicts could redeem by donation;

sentences.zh: 三十四年，有通倉運米捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirty-fourth year, a precedent for donation commutation by transporting grain to the general granaries;
translations.idiomatic: in 1695 commutation by transporting grain to central granaries was allowed;

sentences.zh: 三十九年，有永定河工捐贖例；

translations.literal: in the thirty-ninth year, a precedent for donation commutation for Yongding River works;
translations.idiomatic: in 1700 commutation for Yongding River works was allowed;

sentences.zh: 六十年，有河工捐贖例。

translations.literal: in the sixtieth year, a precedent for donation commutation for river works.
translations.idiomatic: in 1721 commutation for river works was allowed.

sentences.zh: 然皆事竣停止，其歷朝沿用者，惟雍正十二年戶部會同刑部奏准預籌運糧事例，不論旗、民，罪應斬、絞，非常赦所不原者，三品以上官照西安駝捐例捐運糧銀一萬二千兩，四品官照營田例捐運糧銀五千兩，五、六品官照營田例捐銀四千兩，七品以下、進士、舉人二千五百兩，貢、監生二千兩，平人一千二百兩，軍、流各減十分之四，徒以下各減十分之六，俱准免罪。

translations.literal: Yet all were discontinued when the projects ended; the only one continued through successive reigns was the precedent approved in the twelfth year of Yongzheng by joint memorial of the Ministry of Revenue and the Board of Punishments for advance provision of transport grain: regardless of Bannerman or commoner, for offenses warranting decapitation or strangulation not pardoned by extraordinary amnesty, officials of the third rank and above, following the Xi'an camel donation precedent, donated twelve thousand taels of silver for transport grain; fourth-rank officials, following the military colony precedent, five thousand taels; fifth- and sixth-rank officials four thousand taels; seventh rank and below, metropolitan degree holders, and provincial graduates two thousand five hundred taels; tribute students and students of the Imperial Academy two thousand taels; commoners one thousand two hundred taels; military exile and banishment were each reduced by four-tenths, penal servitude and below by six-tenths—all were permitted to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: All ended when projects concluded; only the 1734 precedent for advance grain transport continued. Bannermen and commoners alike guilty of decapitation or strangulation not covered by extraordinary amnesty could commute: third rank and above twelve thousand taels (per the Xi'an camel precedent), fourth rank five thousand, fifth and sixth rank four thousand, seventh rank and below plus jinshi and juren two thousand five hundred, tribute and academy students two thousand, commoners one thousand two hundred; military exile and banishment rates were reduced forty percent, servitude and below sixty percent—all securing exemption from punishment.

sentences.zh: 西安駝捐，行自雍正元年，營田例則五年所定也。

translations.literal: The Xi'an camel donation had been in force since the first year of Yongzheng; the military colony precedent was fixed in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi'an camel donation dated from 1723; the military colony rates were set in 1727.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，西安布政使張若震奏請另定捐贖笞、杖銀數。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong the Xi'an provincial treasurer Zhang Ruozhen memorialized requesting separate fixation of silver amounts for donation commutation of light-bamboo and stick punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1752 Xi'an provincial treasurer Zhang Ruozhen memorialized for separate silver rates for commutation of light-bamboo and stick penalties.

sentences.zh: 經部議，預籌運糧事例，杖、笞與徒罪不分輕重，一例捐贖，究未允協。

translations.literal: After deliberation by the ministries, under the advance transport grain precedent light-bamboo, stick, and penal servitude were not distinguished by severity but commuted by a single rule—this was ultimately not deemed appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries ruled that applying the advance grain transport precedent to light-bamboo, stick, and servitude without distinguishing severity was inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 除犯枷號、杖責者照徒罪捐贖外，酌擬分杖為一等，笞為一等。

translations.literal: Apart from those guilty of wearing the cangue and stick punishment who commuted according to penal servitude rates, it was proposed after deliberation to divide stick beating into one grade category and light-bamboo into one grade category.
translations.idiomatic: Except for cangue wearers and those subject to stick beating, who commuted at penal-servitude rates, the ministries devised separate grade scales for stick beating and light-bamboo punishment.

sentences.zh: 其數，杖視徒遞減，笞視杖遞減。

translations.literal: As for the amounts, stick beating was progressively reduced with reference to penal servitude, and light-bamboo was progressively reduced with reference to stick beating.
translations.idiomatic: The silver amounts decreased stepwise from servitude rates for stick penalties and from stick rates for light-bamboo penalties.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，諭將斬、絞緩決各犯納贖之例永行停止。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, an edict ordered that the precedent for payment commutation for all convicts sentenced to deferred decapitation or strangulation be permanently discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In 1758 an edict permanently abolished payment commutation for convicts held for deferred decapitation or strangulation.

sentences.zh: 遇有恩赦減等時，其憚於遠行者，再准收贖。

translations.literal: When amnesties reduced sentences by grade, those who feared distant travel were again permitted statutory commutation.
translations.idiomatic: When amnesties reduced a sentence, those who dreaded long-distance exile could again commute by payment.

sentences.zh: 而贖鍰則仍視原擬罪名，不得照減等之罪。

translations.literal: But the commutation fine was still calculated according to the originally proposed offense and could not be based on the reduced grade.
translations.idiomatic: The commutation fine, however, still followed the original proposed charge, not the reduced sentence.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: Let this be established as an order.
translations.idiomatic: This was codified as a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 嗣後官員贖罪者，俱照運糧事例核奪。

translations.literal: Thereafter all officials who commuted their offenses were assessed according to the transport grain precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all officials who commuted offenses were assessed under the grain-transport precedent.

sentences.zh: 刑部別設贖罪處，專司其事。

translations.literal: The Board of Punishments separately established an office for offense commutation to manage this exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Punishments set up a separate office devoted solely to offense commutation.

sentences.zh: 此又律贖、例贖而外，別自為制者矣。

translations.literal: This was yet another system established apart from code commutation and sub-statutory commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus donation commutation became a third system, distinct from code commutation and sub-statutory commutation.

sentences.zh: 凌遲，用之十惡中不道以上諸重罪，號為極刑。

translations.literal: Lingchi was applied to such grave offenses among the Ten Abominations as unfilial conduct and above, and was called the extreme punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lingchi applied to the gravest offenses among the Ten Abominations—unfilial conduct and worse—and was regarded as the supreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 梟首，則強盜居多。

translations.literal: Display of the severed head was used mostly for armed robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Display of the severed head was chiefly reserved for armed robbery.

sentences.zh: 戮屍，所以待惡逆及強盜應梟諸犯之監故者。

translations.literal: Corpse dismemberment was reserved for treason and felonious sons, and for prisoners in custody who died through intentional negligence when they should have been executed by decapitation with head displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Corpse dismemberment applied to treason and felonious sons, and to prisoners who died in custody through deliberate neglect when they should have been decapitated with head displayed.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸刑，類皆承用明律，略有通變，行之二百餘年。

translations.literal: All these punishments generally followed the Ming code with slight modifications and were enforced for more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: These punishments largely followed Ming practice with minor adjustments and remained in force for over two centuries.

sentences.zh: 至過誤殺之賠人，竊盜之割腳筋，重辟減等之貫耳鼻，強盜、貪官及窩逃之籍家產，或沿自盛京定例，或順治朝偶行之峻令，不久革除，非所論也。

translations.literal: As for compensation payments for accidental killings, cutting the tendons of the feet for theft, piercing the ears and nose for reduced capital offenses, and confiscation of family property for armed robbery, corrupt officials, and harboring fugitives—some originated in Shenyang regulations, others were severe measures occasionally applied in the Shunzhi reign and soon abolished; these are not discussed here.
translations.idiomatic: Compensation for accidental homicide, cutting foot tendons for theft, ear-and-nose piercing for commuted capital offenses, and confiscation of family property for armed robbery, corrupt officials, and harboring fugitives—some derived from Shenyang precedents, others were harsh Shunzhi-era measures soon repealed—lie outside this discussion.

sentences.zh: 自光緒變法，二十八年，山西巡撫趙爾巽奏請各省通設罪犯習藝所。

translations.literal: From the Guangxu reforms, in the twenty-eighth year, the Shanxi provincial governor Zhao Erxun memorialized requesting that every province establish vocational training institutions for convicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reforms, in 1902 Shanxi governor Zhao Erxun memorialized for vocational training institutions for convicts in every province.

sentences.zh: 經刑部議准，徒犯毋庸發配，按照年限，於本地收所習藝。

translations.literal: After deliberation the Board of Punishments approved it: convicts sentenced to penal servitude need not be sent into assignment but, according to the term of years, were received into local institutions for vocational training.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Punishments approved the plan: servitude convicts would no longer be sent away but would train locally for the prescribed term.

sentences.zh: 軍、流為常赦所不原者，照定例發配，到配一律收所習藝。

translations.literal: For military exile and banishment not pardoned by ordinary amnesty, assignment followed fixed precedent, and upon arrival all were received into institutions for vocational training.
translations.idiomatic: Military exiles and banished convicts not covered by ordinary amnesty were still assigned as before, but upon arrival all entered vocational training.

sentences.zh: 流二千里限工作六年，二千五百里八年，三千里者十年。

translations.literal: Exile of two thousand li was limited to six years of labor; two thousand five hundred li to eight years; three thousand li to ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thousand-li exile meant six years' labor; two-thousand-five-hundred-li eight years; three-thousand-li ten years.

sentences.zh: 遣軍照滿流年限計算，限滿釋放，聽其自謀生計，並准在配所入籍為民。

translations.literal: Frontier deportation and military exile were calculated according to the full statutory exile term; when the term expired they were released, allowed to seek their own livelihood, and permitted to register as commoners at the place of assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier deportees and military exiles served terms equivalent to full statutory exile; when the term ended they were released to make their own living and could register as commoners at their place of assignment.

sentences.zh: 若為常赦所得原者，無論軍、流，俱無庸發配，即在本省收所習藝。

translations.literal: If the offense was pardonable under ordinary amnesty, whether military exile or banishment, none needed actual assignment and all were received into local institutions for vocational training within their home province.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses pardonable under ordinary amnesty, whether military exile or banishment, required no distant assignment; convicts trained locally within their province.

sentences.zh: 工作年限，亦照前科算。

translations.literal: The term of labor was likewise calculated according to the preceding scale.
translations.idiomatic: Labor terms followed the same schedule as above.

sentences.zh: 自此五徒並不發配，即軍、流之發配者，數亦銳減矣。

translations.literal: From this time the five grades of penal servitude were no longer assigned elsewhere, and even among military exile and banishment those actually sent into assignment sharply decreased in number.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all five servitude grades stayed local, and even among military exiles and banished convicts the number actually sent away dropped sharply.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，刑部奏准刪除充軍名目，將附近、近邊，邊遠併入三流，極邊及煙瘴改為安置，仍與當差並行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Board of Punishments memorialized and approved deletion of the category of military exile, merging nearby, near frontier, and distant frontier into the three grades of exile, changing extreme frontier and miasma regions to resettlement, while still applying alongside labor duty.
translations.idiomatic: In 1903 the Board of Punishments abolished military exile as a category, folding nearby, near-frontier, and distant-frontier grades into the three statutory exile grades, converting extreme frontier and miasma regions to resettlement while retaining labor duty.

sentences.zh: 自此五軍第留其二，而刑名亦改變矣。

translations.literal: From this time of the five grades of military exile only two remained, and the nomenclature of punishments also changed.
translations.idiomatic: Of the five military-exile grades only two survived, and penal terminology changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 三十年，劉坤一、張之洞會奏變法第二摺內，有恤刑獄九條。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, in the joint memorial on reform submitted by Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong, the second memorial contained nine articles on leniency in criminal imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1904 Liu Kunyi and Zhang Zhidong's joint reform memorial included nine articles on leniency in criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 其省刑責條內，經法律館議准，笞、杖等罪，仿照外國罰金之法，改為罰銀。

translations.literal: Within the article on reducing corporal punishment, after deliberation the Law Codification Office approved replacing light-bamboo, stick, and similar offenses with silver fines, following foreign models of monetary penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Under the article on reducing corporal punishment, the Law Codification Office approved replacing light-bamboo and stick penalties with silver fines modeled on Western monetary penalties.

sentences.zh: 凡律例內笞刑五，以五錢為一等，至笞五十罰銀二兩五錢，杖六十者改為罰五兩。

translations.literal: For all five grades of light-bamboo punishment in the code and sub-statutes, five cash constituted one grade, up to fifty blows of the light bamboo fined at two taels and five mace of silver; sixty blows of the stick were changed to a fine of five taels.
translations.idiomatic: The five light-bamboo grades were set at five cash per grade, reaching two taels five mace for fifty blows; sixty stick blows became a five-tael fine.

sentences.zh: 每一等加二兩五錢，以次遞加，至杖一百改為罰十五兩而止。

translations.literal: Each grade added two taels and five mace, increasing step by step, until one hundred blows of the stick were changed to a fine of fifteen taels and no more.
translations.idiomatic: Each grade added two taels five mace, up to a maximum of fifteen taels for one hundred stick blows.

sentences.zh: 如無力完納，折為作工。

translations.literal: If unable to pay in full, the fine was converted to labor.
translations.idiomatic: Those unable to pay in full could convert the fine to labor.

sentences.zh: 應罰一兩，折作工四日，以次遞加，至十五兩折作工六十日而止。

translations.literal: One tael due in fine was converted to four days of labor, increasing step by step, until fifteen taels were converted to sixty days of labor and no more.
translations.idiomatic: One tael of fine equaled four days' labor, scaling up to sixty days for a fifteen-tael fine.

sentences.zh: 然竊盜未便罰金，議將犯竊應擬笞罪者，改科工作一月；

translations.literal: Yet for theft monetary fines were not deemed appropriate; it was proposed that thieves liable to light-bamboo punishment be changed to one month of labor;
translations.idiomatic: Theft, however, was deemed unsuitable for monetary fines; thieves liable to light-bamboo punishment would instead serve one month's labor;

sentences.zh: 杖六十者，改科工作兩月；

translations.literal: those liable to sixty blows of the stick were changed to two months of labor;
translations.idiomatic: those liable to sixty stick blows would serve two months;

sentences.zh: 杖七十至一百，每等遞加兩月。

translations.literal: from seventy to one hundred blows of the stick, each grade added two months.
translations.idiomatic: from seventy to one hundred stick blows, each grade added two months.

sentences.zh: 又附片請將軍、流、徒加杖概予寬免，無庸決責。

translations.literal: A supplementary memorial also requested that additional stick blows attached to military exile, banishment, and penal servitude be wholly remitted, with no need to carry out beating.
translations.idiomatic: A supplementary memorial also requested wholesale remission of additional stick blows for military exile, banishment, and servitude.

sentences.zh: 自此而笞、杖二刑廢棄矣。

translations.literal: From this time the two punishments of light-bamboo and stick beating were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Light-bamboo and stick beating were thus abolished.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，修訂法律大臣沈家本等奏請刪除重法數端，略稱：「見行律例款目極繁，而最重之法，亟應先議刪除者，約有三事：一曰凌遲、梟首、戮屍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year the revising law ministers Shen Jiaben and others memorialized requesting deletion of several heavy punishments, stating in summary: "The articles of the current code and sub-statutes are extremely numerous, and among the heaviest punishments those that urgently should be discussed for deletion number roughly three: first, lingchi, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: In 1905 revising law ministers Shen Jiaben and others memorialized to abolish several severe punishments, noting: "Current statutes are vast, but three exceptionally harsh penalties should be removed first: lingchi, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 凌遲之刑，唐以前無此名目。

translations.literal: The punishment of lingchi had no such name before the Tang dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Lingchi did not exist as a named punishment before the Tang.

sentences.zh: 遼史刑法志始列入正刑之內。

translations.literal: The penal monograph of the History of Liao first listed it among the orthodox punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The penal monograph of the History of Liao first listed it among formal statutory punishments.

sentences.zh: 宋自熙寧以後，漸亦沿用。

translations.literal: From the Xining era of the Song onward it was gradually adopted as well.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song Xining era onward it gradually came into use.

sentences.zh: 元、明至今，相仍未改。

translations.literal: From Yuan and Ming down to the present it has continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan and Ming times to the present it remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 梟首在秦、漢時惟用諸夷族之誅，六朝梁、陳、齊、周諸律，始於斬之外別立梟名。

translations.literal: Display of the severed head in Qin and Han was used only for extermination of the clan; in the Six Dynasties the codes of Liang, Chen, Qi, and Zhou first established the separate category of head display beyond decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin and Han, display of the severed head applied only to clan extermination; Six Dynasties codes of Liang, Chen, Qi, and Zhou first made it a separate penalty beyond decapitation.

sentences.zh: 自隋迄元，復棄而不用。

translations.literal: From Sui through Yuan it was again abandoned and not used.
translations.idiomatic: From Sui through Yuan it fell out of use again.

sentences.zh: 今之斬梟，仍明制也。

translations.literal: Today's decapitation with head displayed still follows the Ming system.
translations.idiomatic: Today's decapitation with head displayed still follows Ming practice.

sentences.zh: 戮屍一事，惟秦時成蟜軍反，其軍吏皆斬戮屍，見於始皇本紀。

translations.literal: As for corpse dismemberment, only when Prince Cheng Jiao's army rebelled in Qin were his military officers all decapitated and their corpses dismembered, as recorded in the Basic Annals of the First Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Corpse dismemberment appears only once in early records: when Prince Cheng Jiao's army rebelled in Qin, his officers were decapitated and their corpses dismembered, as recorded in the First Emperor's annals.

sentences.zh: 此外歷代刑制，俱無此法。

translations.literal: Apart from this, penal systems of successive dynasties all lacked this punishment.
translations.idiomatic: No other dynasty's penal system included this punishment.

sentences.zh: 明自萬曆十六年，定有戮屍條例，專指謀殺祖父母、父母而言。

translations.literal: From the sixteenth year of Wanli in the Ming a sub-statute on corpse dismemberment was fixed, referring specifically to plotting to kill grandparents or parents.
translations.idiomatic: In 1588 the Ming fixed a corpse-dismemberment statute specifically for plotting to kill grandparents or parents.

sentences.zh: 國朝因之，後更推及於強盜。

translations.literal: Our dynasty followed this, and later extended it further to armed robbery.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing followed suit and later extended it to armed robbery.

sentences.zh: 凡此酷重之刑，固所以懲戒兇惡。

translations.literal: All these cruelly heavy punishments were indeed intended to chastise the vicious and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: These cruelly severe punishments were meant to chastise the vicious.

sentences.zh: 第刑至於斬，身首分離，已為至慘。

translations.literal: But when punishment reached decapitation, with body and head separated, it was already the utmost cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet decapitation already severed body from head—the utmost cruelty.

sentences.zh: 若命在頃忽，菹醢必令備嘗，氣久消亡，刀鋸猶難倖免，揆諸仁人之心，當必慘然不樂。

translations.literal: If life lasts but a moment, yet mincing and dismemberment must all be tasted in full; long after breath has vanished, knife and saw still cannot be escaped—measured against the heart of a humane person, this must surely inspire grief and displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: When life lasts but a moment yet the condemned must endure every form of mincing and dissection, and long after death knife and saw still mutilate the corpse, any humane heart must recoil in horror.

sentences.zh: 謂將以懲本犯，而被刑者魂魄何知；

translations.literal: If one says it is to punish the principal offender, what could the executed person's soul know?
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is to punish the offender, what could the dead know?

sentences.zh: 謂將以警戒眾人，而習見習聞，轉感召其殘忍之性，實非聖世所宜遵。

translations.literal: If one says it is to warn the multitude, yet through constant sight and hearing it instead summons forth their cruel nature—this is truly not what a sage age should follow.
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is to warn the public, habitual exposure to such cruelty only nurtures brutality—hardly fitting for an enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 請將凌遲、梟首、戮屍三項，一概刪除，死罪至斬決而止。

translations.literal: We request that the three items of lingchi, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment be wholly deleted, and that capital punishment stop at immediate decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: We request abolition of lingchi, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment, limiting capital punishment to immediate decapitation.

sentences.zh: 凡律例內凌遲、斬梟各條，俱改斬決。

translations.literal: All articles in the code and sub-statutes on lingchi and decapitation with head displayed should be changed to immediate decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: All code and sub-statute articles prescribing lingchi or decapitation with head displayed should be changed to immediate decapitation.

sentences.zh: 斬決而下，依次遞減。

translations.literal: Below immediate decapitation, punishments should be reduced step by step in order.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser penalties below immediate decapitation should be reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 一曰緣坐。

translations.literal: Second: guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: Second: guilt by association.

sentences.zh: 緣坐之制，起於秦之參夷及收司連坐法。

translations.literal: The institution of guilt by association originated in Qin practices of collective extermination and joint punishment of related officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt by association originated in Qin practices of clan extermination and joint punishment of related officials.

sentences.zh: 漢高後除三族令，文帝除收孥相坐律，當時以為盛德。

translations.literal: Empress Lü of Han abolished the decree on extermination of three clans; Emperor Wen abolished the law on seizing wives and children for joint punishment—at the time these were regarded as great acts of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü abolished clan extermination; Emperor Wen ended the seizure of wives and children for joint punishment—both hailed as great acts of mercy.

sentences.zh: 惜夷族之誅，猶間用之。

translations.literal: Regrettably, extermination of the clan was still occasionally applied.
translations.idiomatic: Clan extermination regrettably persisted in occasional use.

sentences.zh: 晉以下仍有家屬從坐之法，唐律惟反叛、惡逆、不道，律有緣坐，他無有也。

translations.literal: From Jin onward there remained laws for family members to share punishment; in the Tang Code only rebellion, felonious sons, and unfilial conduct had guilt by association in the code—nothing else did.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin onward families could still share punishment, but Tang law limited guilt by association to rebellion, felonious sons, and unfilial conduct alone.

sentences.zh: 今律則奸黨、交結近侍諸項俱緣坐矣，反獄、邪教諸項亦緣坐矣。

translations.literal: In today's code, factionalism, collusion with palace attendants, and similar items all involve guilt by association; prison revolt, heterodox sects, and similar items also involve guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: Today's code extends guilt by association to factionalism, collusion with palace attendants, prison revolt, heterodox sects, and more.

sentences.zh: 一案株連，動輒數十人。

translations.literal: In a single case implicated persons often numbered dozens.
translations.idiomatic: A single case could implicate dozens of people.

sentences.zh: 夫以一人之故而波及全家，以無罪之人而科以重罪，漢文帝以為不正之法反害於民，北魏崔挺嘗曰『一人有罪，延及闔門，則司馬牛受桓魋之罰，柳下惠膺盜跖之誅，不亦哀哉』，其言皆篤論也。

translations.literal: To involve an entire family because of one person's offense, and to impose heavy punishment on the innocent—Emperor Wen of Han regarded such improper law as harmful to the people; Cui Ting of Northern Wei once said, "When one person is guilty and the whole household is implicated, then Sima Niu would suffer Huan Tui's punishment and Liu Xiahui would bear Zhi's execution—is this not lamentable?"—all such words are sound judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing an entire family for one person's crime and imposing heavy penalties on the innocent—Emperor Wen of Han called such law harmful to the people; Cui Ting of Northern Wei wrote that when one person's guilt reaches the whole household, "Sima Niu would suffer Huan Tui's punishment and Liu Xiahui would bear Zhi's execution—is this not lamentable?"—sound judgment all.

sentences.zh: 今世各國，皆主持刑罰止及一身之義，與『罪人不孥』之古訓實相符合。

translations.literal: All nations today uphold the principle that punishment extends only to the person himself, which truly accords with the ancient teaching that "punishment does not reach the offender's children."
translations.idiomatic: Modern nations uphold punishment limited to the offender alone, in keeping with the ancient teaching that guilt does not extend to one's family.

sentences.zh: 請將律內緣坐各條，除知情者仍坐罪外，其不知情者悉予寬免。

translations.literal: We request that in all articles on guilt by association in the code, except those who knew of the offense and are still punished, all who did not know be wholly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: We request that guilt-by-association articles punish only those who knew of the offense; all who did not know should be exempted.

sentences.zh: 餘條有科及家屬者准此。

translations.literal: Other articles that impose punishment on family members should follow this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Other articles imposing penalties on family members should follow the same rule.

sentences.zh: 一曰刺字。

translations.literal: Third: tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Third: tattooing.

sentences.zh: 刺字乃古墨刑，漢之黥也。

translations.literal: Tattooing was the ancient ink punishment—the branding of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing was the ancient ink punishment—the Han-era branding penalty.

sentences.zh: 文帝廢肉刑而黥亦廢，魏、晉、六朝雖有逃奴劫盜之刺，旋行旋廢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen abolished corporal punishment and branding was abolished as well; though Wei, Jin, and the Six Dynasties occasionally tattooed runaway slaves and robbers, the practice was adopted and abandoned in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen abolished corporal punishment and branding with it; Wei, Jin, and Six Dynasties occasionally tattooed runaway slaves and robbers, but the practice came and went.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐皆無此法。

translations.literal: Sui and Tang both lacked this punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Sui nor Tang law included tattooing.

sentences.zh: 至石晉天福間，始創刺配之制，相沿至今。

translations.literal: Only in the Tianfu era of Later Jin was the system of tattooing combined with exile first created, and it has continued down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jin's Tianfu era first combined tattooing with exile—a practice that continued to the present.

sentences.zh: 其初不過竊盜逃人，其後日加煩密。

translations.literal: At first it applied only to thieves and fugitives; later it grew daily more elaborate and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Initially it applied only to thieves and fugitives; later it grew ever more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 在立法之意，原欲使莠民知恥，庶幾悔過而遷善。

translations.literal: In the legislative intent, the original aim was to make wicked commoners know shame, so that they might repent and turn to goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The original intent was to shame habitual offenders into repentance and reform.

sentences.zh: 詎知習於為非者，適予以標識，助其兇橫。

translations.literal: Who could have known that those habituated to wrongdoing would instead be given a mark that aided their ferocity and arrogance?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for habitual criminals the mark became a badge of defiance, fueling their brutality.

sentences.zh: 而偶罹法網者，則黥刺一膺，終身僇辱。

translations.literal: Yet those who chanced to fall into the net of the law, once branded on the chest, suffered lifelong shame and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fell into the law's net by misfortune bore a chest tattoo and lifelong disgrace.

sentences.zh: 夫肉刑久廢，而此法獨存，漢文所謂刻肌膚痛而不德者，未能收弼教之益，而徒留此不德之名，豈仁政所宜出此。

translations.literal: Corporal punishment was long abolished, yet this law alone remained—what Han Emperor Wen called cutting the flesh and causing pain without virtue; it failed to achieve the benefit of assisting instruction, and only left this name for lack of virtue—how could humane governance produce such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishment was long abolished, yet tattooing alone survived—what Emperor Wen called "cutting flesh and causing pain without virtue." It aided neither reform nor instruction but left only a stain on humane governance.

sentences.zh: 擬請將刺字款目，概行刪除。

translations.literal: It is proposed to delete all articles on tattooing entirely.
translations.idiomatic: We propose abolishing all tattooing provisions.

sentences.zh: 凡竊盜皆令收所習藝，按罪名輕重，定以年限，俾一技能嫻，得以餬口，自少再犯、三犯之人。

translations.literal: All thieves should be received into vocational training institutions; according to the severity of the offense a term of years should be fixed, so that once a skill is mastered they may earn a living, thereby reducing repeat and third-time offenders.
translations.idiomatic: All thieves should enter vocational training for terms scaled to offense severity, mastering a trade to earn a living and reducing repeat offenders.

sentences.zh: 一切遞解人犯，嚴令地方官僉差押解，果能實力奉行，逃亡者自少也。」

translations.literal: For all convicts forwarded under escort, local officials should be strictly ordered to assign personnel for guarded transport; if this were truly enforced, fugitives would naturally be fewer."
translations.idiomatic: Local officials should strictly escort all forwarded convicts; if enforced, escapes would naturally decline."

sentences.zh: 奏上，諭令凌遲、梟首、戮屍三項永遠刪除。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered that the three items of lingchi, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment be permanently deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved, and an edict permanently abolished lingchi, display of the severed head, and corpse dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 所有現行律例內凌遲、斬梟各條，俱改為斬決；

translations.literal: All current articles in the code and sub-statutes on lingchi and decapitation with head displayed were changed to immediate decapitation;
translations.idiomatic: All current articles prescribing lingchi or decapitation with head displayed were changed to immediate decapitation;

sentences.zh: 其斬決各條，俱改為絞決；

translations.literal: all articles on immediate decapitation were changed to immediate strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: all articles on immediate decapitation were changed to immediate strangulation;

sentences.zh: 絞決各條，俱改為絞監候，入於秋審情實；

translations.literal: all articles on immediate strangulation were changed to strangulation held in custody for review, entering the autumn assizes as cases of true culpability;
translations.idiomatic: all articles on immediate strangulation were changed to strangulation held for autumn review as cases of true culpability;

sentences.zh: 斬監候各條，俱改為絞監候，與絞候人犯仍入於秋審，分別實緩。

translations.literal: all articles on decapitation held in custody for review were changed to strangulation held in custody for review, and together with those held for strangulation they still entered the autumn assizes, classified as true culpability or reprieve.
translations.idiomatic: all articles on decapitation held for review were changed to strangulation held for review; both entered the autumn assizes, classified as true culpability or reprieve.

sentences.zh: 至緣坐各條，除知情者仍治罪外，餘悉寬免。

translations.literal: As for all articles on guilt by association, except those who knew of the offense and were still punished, the rest were wholly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt-by-association articles punished only those who knew of the offense; all others were exempted.

sentences.zh: 其刺字等項，亦概行革除。

translations.literal: Tattooing and similar items were also wholly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooing and similar provisions were also abolished.

sentences.zh: 旨下，中外稱頌焉。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, it was praised within and beyond the court.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, it was widely praised at court and throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，法律館奏准將戲殺、誤殺、擅殺虛擬死罪各案，分別減為徒、流。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the Law Codification Office memorialized and approved reducing cases of playful killing, accidental killing, and unauthorized killing nominally charged as capital offenses, respectively, to penal servitude and exile.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906 the Law Codification Office approved reducing playful killing, accidental killing, and unauthorized killing—cases nominally capital—to servitude or exile.

sentences.zh: 自此而死刑亦多輕減矣。

translations.literal: From this time capital punishment was also greatly lightened in many cases.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was thus substantially lightened.

sentences.zh: 又是年法律館以婦女收贖，銀數太微，不足以資警戒，議准婦女犯笞、杖，照新章罰金。

translations.literal: In the same year the Law Codification Office, finding that statutory commutation for women involved too small an amount of silver to serve as a warning, approved that women guilty of light-bamboo and stick offenses be fined according to the new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Law Codification Office found women's commutation rates too low to deter offense and approved fines for women guilty of light-bamboo or stick offenses under the new regulations.

sentences.zh: 徒、流、軍、遣，除不孝及奸、盜、詐偽舊例應實發者，改留本地習藝所工作，以十年為限，餘俱准其贖罪。

translations.literal: For penal servitude, exile, military exile, and frontier deportation, except unfilial conduct and adultery, theft, and fraud where old precedent required actual assignment, convicts were changed to labor at local vocational training institutions for a limit of ten years; all others were permitted to commute their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: For servitude, exile, military exile, and frontier deportation—except unfilial conduct, adultery, theft, and fraud requiring actual assignment—women would labor locally at vocational training institutions for up to ten years; all others could commute.

sentences.zh: 徒一年折銀二十兩，每五兩為一等，五徒准此遞加。

translations.literal: One year of penal servitude was converted to twenty taels of silver; every five taels constituted one grade, and the five grades of servitude increased accordingly step by step.
translations.idiomatic: One year of servitude converted to twenty taels; each five-tael increment applied across all five servitude grades.

sentences.zh: 由徒入流，每一等加十兩，三流准此遞加。

translations.literal: From servitude into exile, each grade added ten taels, and the three grades of exile increased accordingly step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Moving from servitude to exile, each grade added ten taels across all three exile grades.

sentences.zh: 遣、軍照滿流科斷。

translations.literal: Frontier deportation and military exile were sentenced according to the full statutory exile scale.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier deportation and military exile were assessed at full statutory exile rates.

sentences.zh: 如無力完繳，將應罰之數，照新章按銀數折算時日，改習工藝。

translations.literal: If unable to pay in full, the amount due was converted to days according to the new regulations based on the silver amount, and changed to vocational training.
translations.idiomatic: Those unable to pay in full could convert the fine to vocational training under the new silver-to-days schedule.

sentences.zh: 其犯該枷號，不論日數多寡，俱酌加五兩，以示區別。

translations.literal: For those liable to the cangue, regardless of the number of days, five taels were added after deliberation to show distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Cangue offenders, regardless of term length, paid an additional five taels to distinguish their cases.

sentences.zh: 自此而收贖銀數亦稍變矣。

translations.literal: From this time the silver amounts for statutory commutation also changed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory commutation rates also shifted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 故宣統二年頒布之現行刑律，第將近數年奏定之章程採獲修入，於是刑制遂大有變更。

translations.literal: Thus the current penal code promulgated in the second year of Xuantong merely gathered and revised into it the regulations memorialized and fixed in recent years, and thereby the penal system underwent great change.
translations.idiomatic: The penal code promulgated in 1910 incorporated regulations fixed over recent years, bringing sweeping change to the penal system.

sentences.zh: 其五刑之目，首罰刑十，以代舊律之笞、杖。

translations.literal: Among the categories of the five punishments, first came ten grades of monetary penalty, replacing the light-bamboo and stick beating of the old code.
translations.idiomatic: The five punishments now began with ten grades of monetary penalty, replacing the old light-bamboo and stick penalties.

sentences.zh: 一等罰，罰銀五錢，至十等罰，為銀十五兩，據法律館議覆恤刑獄之奏也。

translations.literal: The first grade of penalty fined five mace of silver; the tenth grade was fifteen taels—according to the Law Codification Office's deliberated reply to the memorial on leniency in criminal imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: The first grade fined five mace of silver; the tenth fifteen taels—following the Law Codification Office's response to the memorial on leniency in criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 次徒刑五，年限仍舊律。

translations.literal: Next came the five grades of penal servitude, with terms still following the old code.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five grades of penal servitude, with terms unchanged from the old code.

sentences.zh: 次流刑三，道里仍舊律，然均不加杖，以法律館業經附片奏刪也。

translations.literal: Next came the three grades of exile, with distances still following the old code, yet in each case no additional stick blows were added, because the Law Codification Office had already memorialized in a supplementary document requesting their deletion.
translations.idiomatic: Next came three grades of exile at the old distances, but without additional stick blows—the Law Codification Office had already secured their removal by supplementary memorial.

sentences.zh: 次遣刑二：曰極邊足四千里及煙瘴地方安置，曰新疆當差。

translations.literal: Next came two grades of deportation: assignment to the extreme frontier at a full four thousand li and to miasma regions, and service in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Next came two deportation grades: resettlement at the extreme frontier or in miasma regions four thousand li distant, and labor service in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 以閏刑加入正刑，承用者廣，不得不別自為制也。

translations.literal: Because intercalary punishments were incorporated into the orthodox punishments and widely applied, they had to be given a separate system of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Because supplementary penalties had been folded into the formal punishments and widely applied, they required a separate statutory framework.

sentences.zh: 次死刑二：曰絞，曰斬。

translations.literal: Next came the two capital punishments: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment comprised two forms: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 時雖有死刑唯一之議，以舊制顯分等差，且凌遲、梟首等項甫經議減，不敢徑行廢斬也。

translations.literal: Although at the time there was discussion of a single form of capital punishment, the old system clearly distinguished grades, and lingchi, head display, and the like had only just been debated for reduction—decapitation could not be abolished outright.
translations.idiomatic: Although some argued for a single capital penalty, the old system clearly distinguished grades, and with lingchi and head display only recently curtailed, decapitation could not be abolished outright.

sentences.zh: 徒、流雖仍舊律，然為制不同。

translations.literal: Penal servitude and exile still followed the old code in name, yet the institution differed.
translations.idiomatic: Servitude and exile retained the old statutory labels but operated under a different system.

sentences.zh: 按照習藝章程，五徒依限收入本地習藝所習藝；

translations.literal: According to the vocational training regulations, all five grades of servitude were admitted within the term to local vocational training institutes for instruction in a trade;
translations.idiomatic: Under the vocational training regulations, all five servitude grades were admitted to local training institutes within the statutory term;

sentences.zh: 流、遣毋論發配與否，俱應工作。

translations.literal: for exile and deportation, whether or not assignment to a distant place was required, labor was obligatory in every case.
translations.idiomatic: exile and deportation, whether or not distant assignment was required, always entailed labor.

sentences.zh: 故於徒五等註明按限工作，流二千里注工作六年，二千五百里注工作八年，三千里注工作十年，遣刑俱注工作十二年。

translations.literal: Therefore the five grades of servitude were annotated with labor within the term; exile of two thousand li was annotated with six years of labor, two thousand five hundred li with eight years, three thousand li with ten years, and all deportation with twelve years of labor.
